messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm putting together a new Grafana panel to spot GPU hotspots across regions (util, mem, temp, power). Need a heatmap that surfaces per-node sustained thermal spikes and alloc fragmentation. Anyone available to review queries?

raj: +1, want this ASAP — we've seen weird temp spikes in us-west-2 during nightly provisioning. A heatmap + per-pod streaming tail would help.

linh: Can you paste the PromQL you're thinking? Might need to use label_join for instance->region mapping.

maya: draft PromQLs below. open to edits:

```
# GPU temperature 1m avg per instance
avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_temp_celsius[1m]) by (instance)

# GPU memory utilization percentage
(1 - (sum(gpu_memory_free_bytes) by (instance) / sum(gpu_memory_total_bytes) by (instance))) * 100
```

olivia: For heatmap, use `instance` on y and `gpu_index` on x, plus `region` var. Also add `irate(gpu_power_draw_watts[1m])` for spikes.

sam (eng-sre): FYI alerts: current temp alert at >85C for 2m fires too often during warmups. Suggest change to >88C for 3m and add suppression for nodes tagged `provisioning=true`.

maya: good point. propose thresholds: temp >90 for 5m as Sev3, 88-90 for 10m warning. Also create annotation panel for deploys — grafana-bot should post deploy tags.

grafana-bot: deploy annotated: prod-deploy v1.8.2 by @ci on 1759204400

raj: we also need to handle missing metrics during network blips — prometheus shows `up{job="nvidia-exporter"} = 0` for a minute. Maybe display `up` as small sparkline under each instance.

linh: Agree. Also add a panel for `gpu_kv_cache_hit_rate` to see inference cache effects on memory.

olivia: Will wire up a template var `region` and `cluster` and add a panel that aggregates by `node_pool` so SRE can scope by Dedicated vs Hosted.

maya: Thanks all — I'll push a draft dashboard in `grafana/dashboards/gpu-fleet-hotspots.json` and tag you. If no objections, I'll land the alert rule change in `/infra/alerts/gpu-thermals.yaml`.

raj: lgtm, cc @oncall for visibility :eyes: 

sam (eng-sre): quick log snippet from one affected node:
```
Mar 08 03:12:22 node-342 exporter[1234]: scrape timeout
Mar 08 03:12:23 node-342 kubelet: pod kube-provisioner restarted
Mar 08 03:12:28 node-342 nvidia-smi: Driver lost
```

maya: I'll add a note to dashboard description: "shows suspected provisioning-related noise; use `provisioning=true` filter". Landing after review.
